chapter: A musical family and the old New Orleans bands
title: The Tennessee Ten, Florence Mills and Little Broadway Rastus
summary: Danny describes the Tennessee Ten revue, Florence Mills and the sliding drummer Rastus, and notes it played the Orpheum rather than TOBA.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Yeah, Danny, to continue our conversation about the early days: You mentioned the vaudeville act, the Tennessee Ten. What did they do?

Well, when I got to New York, I found out about the Tennessee Ten. I forget the name of the people. But Florence Mills was the star. She later starred in The Blackbirds. Florence Mills was one of the stars, dancers of the girl performers, what you call a soubrette. She came out front and she done her thing, and she danced with the little chorus there. There was ten people, but they were very compact, what you would call a revue, a small revue or a small tab show. You could play the side-show in a carnival. You could go in a nightclub in town and do an

act, a compact hour act. But they generally did, like twenty minutes or thirty minutes on the Orpheum and the Pantages circuit. It was considered one of the greatest acts. And especially when you mention this name of Florence Mills. She later became one of the greatest Black performers there ever was. And you mention her in awe when you say "Florence Mills." She lit up a stage. She had this charisma that people have, when you see them they just upset a stage, and it's natural. That was Florence Mills.

That was the Tennessee Ten. They had Little Broadway Rastus, who was a terrific drummer. They speak of him. He went to Europe and stayed over there. He could run and jump and slide, slide and sort of... It was mystifying how he could run across the stage and slide, and made a spread eagle on the stage, and just continued to move. When you'd look at the momentum to think he had stopped, he'd slide some more.
You know, like a rubber band pullin' him. Yeah, yeah. And he later... Later on I saw him with a septet. I can't think of the name of that septet. They were great in vaudeville.
But the Tennessee Ten was one of the greatest acts in vaudeville. They played the big-time Orpheum circuit.
Never went on the TOBA circuit, which was the Black ...(?)... attraction. It was Tough On Black Asses; that was the name of TOBA. It started at the Pekin Theatre and went down South.
